transcript.text: roomba e5 wont charge properly, sometimes it does sometimes it doesnt

Intermittent charging is most often a contact issue: dirt on the metal charging pads, the robot not quite seating on the dock, or a marginal dock/socket connection. If those are sound, an ageing battery or a fault in the dock/charging circuit becomes more likely. 1. Switch the dock off at the wall and unplug it. Wipe the metal charging contacts on the underside of the Roomba and on the dock with a dry, lint-free cloth. Check for dust, oxidation or anything preventing the robot sitting flat. Reconnect it and place the robot squarely on the dock. If it then charges reliably, the contact connection was the cause. 2. Check the dock lead is pushed fully home at both ends and try the dock in another known-working wall socket. Do not use an extension lead for this test if possible. If charging changes when the socket or lead is moved, suspect the dock power supply/lead. 3. Put the dock on a hard, level floor with clear space around it, then send or place the robot onto it. A dock on thick carpet or one that can slide can leave the contacts only partly connected. When it fails to charge, does the dock’s power light show and what does the Roomba’s charge/status light do after you place it on the dock? That will help separate a dock-power problem from contacts or the battery.
dock power light comes on when it docks. robot light ring goes red when it fails and the app says Charging error 5

I can’t confirm the exact meaning of “Charging error 5” for an E5 from the available code information, so I would not treat it as proof of one particular failed part. With the dock light coming on, the main possibilities are still poor contact between robot and dock, a weak dock charging output, or the battery. 1. Unplug the dock. Wipe the metal contact pads underneath the Roomba and on the dock with a dry lint-free cloth. Check the dock contacts move freely and spring back if they are spring-loaded; remove any dust or film. This is the commonest cause of intermittent charging. 2. Plug the dock directly into a known-good wall socket and place the robot squarely on a hard, level floor at the dock. Watch whether it begins charging normally or immediately returns to the red ring/error. If moving or reseating it changes the result, it points strongly to the contacts or docking position. If the contacts are clean and it still gives the same error even when carefully seated, the battery or dock/charging electronics becomes more likely. That normally needs diagnosis or replacement of the faulty unit rather than further external adjustment.
ok i wiped the contacts, they were grubby with a greasy film and loads of hair. charged every night for 4 days now, no error. dock is on carpet by the sofa a bit wonky tho. no heat or smell from it

That points strongly to the greasy film and hair on the charging contacts being the cause. Keep the dock on as firm and level a surface as practical; moving it off the wonky carpet onto hard flooring would make docking more consistent. Give both sets of contacts a quick dry wipe whenever you empty/clean the robot, especially if hair builds up. No heat or smell is reassuring. If Charging Error 5 returns despite clean contacts and a level dock, then the dock output or battery would be the next suspects, but for now this is resolved.

candidates: Dirty or poorly aligned charging contacts/dock connection (high)
Dock power supply or wall socket connection (medium)
Ageing battery or charging fault within the robot/dock (medium)
